rows.verified: HSE guidance on woodworking machinery is aimed at employers, dutyholders, managers and supervisors responsible for safe use.
The guidance applies to most woodworking machinery but excludes hand-held tools.
It covers work with wood, corkboard, fibreboard and composite materials.
Woodworking dutyholders must provide suitable information and instruction.
Workers must receive appropriate training for the machinery and tasks they perform.
Machinery must have suitable guarding and protective measures.
PUWER duties apply to organisations whose employees use work equipment whether the organisation owns the equipment or not.
Safe-use arrangements should reflect the machine, material, task and foreseeable misuse.
Woodworking risk depends on machine type, cutter, feed method, guarding, extraction, material, maintenance and operator competence.
Woodworking evidence is machine-, task-, safeguard-, operator-, material- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
The Pressure Systems Safety Regulations aim to prevent serious injury from stored-energy release after pressure-system failure.
Users and owners must know the safe operating limits of pressure equipment.
Most pressure systems require a suitable written scheme of examination before operation.
The written scheme should be drawn up or certified as suitable by a competent person.
The scheme must cover protective devices, pressure vessels and dangerous parts of pipework where failure could create danger.
The written scheme must specify the nature and frequency of examinations and any special preparation measures.
Statutory examination does not replace regular inspection and routine maintenance.
People who operate, install, maintain, repair, inspect or test pressure equipment need appropriate training and refresher training.
Pressure-system risk depends on fluid, pressure, volume, temperature, design, protective devices, deterioration, maintenance and operating conditions.
Pressure-system evidence is equipment-, fluid-, duty-, examination-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
